name_translation: The Yoga of the Field and the Knower of the Field

verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च |
एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च |
एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca |
etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca keśava || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; prakṛtim—material nature; puruṣam—the conscious enjoyer/soul; ca eva—and also; kṣetram—the field (body/matter); kṣetra-jñam—the knower of the field; eva ca—and also; etat—these; veditum—to understand; icchāmi—I desire; jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; ca—and; keśava—O Krishna (slayer of Keshi).
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Prakriti (nature) and Purusha (the spirit), the Field (Kshetra) and the Knower of the Field (Kshetrajna), Knowledge (Jnana) and the Object of Knowledge (Jneya)—these, O Keshava, I desire to understand.
verses.meaning: Chapter 13 commences the third and final sextet (Tritiya Shatka) of the Bhagavad Gita (Chapters 13–18), which is predominantly dedicated to Jnana Yoga—metaphysical discrimination and transcendental philosophy. Arjuna opens with six fundamental philosophical categories: Prakriti (matter/energy), Purusha (the conscious observer), Kshetra (the physical and psychophysical field), Kshetrajna (the knower of the field), Jnana (the spiritual disciplines that unveil reality), and Jneya (Parabrahman, the Supreme Reality to be known). Sri Krishna addresses each of these foundational pillars in systematic depth.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते |
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते |
एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate |
etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; idam—this; śarīram—body; kaunteya—O son of Kunti (Arjuna); kṣetram—the field; iti—thus; abhidhīyate—is called; etat—this; yaḥ—whoever; vetti—knows/observes; tam—him; prāhuḥ—they call; kṣetra-jñaḥ—the knower of the field; iti—thus; tat-vidaḥ—those who know the truth (the seers).
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: This body, O Kaunteya, is called the Field (Kshetra), and he who knows it is called the Knower of the Field (Kshetrajna) by the wise seers of truth.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna defines the first two categories. The psycho-physical mechanism (the gross, subtle, and causal bodies) is designated as 'Kshetra' (the Field) because, like agricultural soil, actions (karma) are sown as seeds, sprout, and yield their harvest of joys and sorrows. The conscious entity that observes, experiences, and is aware of this body-mind complex is 'Kshetrajna' (the Knower of the Field). The seer is distinct from the seen; the observer is never identical to the instrument of observation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata |
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: kṣetra-jñam—the Knower of the field; ca api—and also; mām—Me (the Supreme Lord); viddhi—know; sarva-kṣetreṣu—in all fields; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna); kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ—of the field and the knower of the field; jñānam—knowledge; yat—which; tat—that; jñānam—true knowledge; matam—opinion/verdict; mama—My.
verses.translation: Know Me also, O Bharata, as the Supreme Knower (Kshetrajna) dwelling in all fields. The knowledge of the field and its knower—this alone is true knowledge in My estimation.
verses.meaning: This is one of the most profound metaphysical revelations in the Gita. While each individual soul (Jivatman) is the knower of its particular individual field, Sri Krishna proclaims that He, the Supreme Lord (Paramatman), is the Universal Knower residing simultaneously within all fields throughout creation. True spiritual wisdom (Jnana) does not consist in mere intellectual analysis of material nature, but in discriminating between perishable matter (Kshetra), the individual soul (Jivatman), and the Supreme Indweller (Paramatman).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् |
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् |
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे शृणु || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛkca yadvikāri yataśca yat |
sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śṛṇu || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: tat—that; kṣetram—field; yat—what; ca—and; yādṛk—of what nature; ca—and; yat-vikāri—what its modifications are; yataḥ—whence; ca—and; yat—what; saḥ—he (the Knower); ca—and; yaḥ—who; yat-prabhāvaḥ—what his powers are; ca—and; tat—that; samāsena—in brief; me—from Me; śṛṇu—hear.
verses.translation: Hear now from Me in brief what that Field is, what its nature is, what its modifications are, whence it arises, who that Knower is, and what His powers are.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna lays down the structured agenda for the subsequent verses. He will systematically delineate the constituent elements of matter, the psychological modifications of the mind, the origin of cosmic manifestation, and the transcendental majesty and omnipotence of the indwelling Knower.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् |
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् |
ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्चितैः || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak |
brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniścitaiḥ || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: ṛṣibhiḥ—by the seers/sages; bahudhā—in manifold ways; gītam—has been sung; chandobhiḥ—by Vedic hymns; vividhaiḥ—various; pṛthak—distinctly; brahma-sūtra-padaiḥ—by the aphorisms of the Brahma Sutras; ca eva—and also; hetumadbhiḥ—endowed with logical reasoning; viniścitaiḥ—definitive/conclusive.
verses.translation: This truth has been sung in manifold ways by the ancient sages, chanted distinctly in various Vedic hymns, and articulated in the aphorisms of the Brahma Sutras with rigorous reasoning and definitive conviction.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna cites the threefold authority of Vedic revelation: the spiritual realizations of ancient Rishis (Anubhuti), the revealed chants of the Vedas/Upanishads (Shruti), and the logical, philosophical aphorisms of the Brahma Sutras (Nyaya/Yukti). The teaching of the Bhagavad Gita is not an isolated doctrine, but the supreme synthesis of all Vedic wisdom.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च |
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च |
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca |
indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: mahā-bhūtāni—the five great cosmic elements (earth, water, fire, air, ether); ahaṅkāraḥ—the ego-sense/false ego; buddhiḥ—the intellect; avyaktam—the unmanifest primordial nature (Prakriti); eva ca—and also; indriyāṇi daśa ekam—the ten senses (five of perception, five of action) and the one mind; ca—and; pañca—the five; ca—and; indriya-gocarāḥ—the objects of the senses (sound, touch, form, taste, smell).
verses.translation: The five great elements (Mahabhutas), the ego-sense (Ahankara), the intellect (Buddhi), the unmanifest primal matter (Avyakta), the ten senses and the one mind, and the five objects of the senses;
verses.meaning: Verses 6 and 7 enumerate the 24 cosmic tattvas (principles) of Sankhya philosophy that constitute the Field (Kshetra): 5 gross elements + ego + intellect + unmanifest root-matter (Avyakta) + 5 knowledge-gathering senses (Jnanendriyas) + 5 working organs (Karmendriyas) + the mind (Manas) + 5 sense objects (Tanmatras/Vishayas). All of these belong to the objective realm of matter.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः |
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः |
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanā dhṛtiḥ |
etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: icchā—desire; dveṣaḥ—aversion; sukham—pleasure; duḥkham—pain; saṅghātaḥ—the aggregate bodily organism; cetanā—reflected consciousness/mental alertness; dhṛtiḥ—fortitude/will; etat—this; kṣetram—the field; samāsena—briefly; sa-vikāram—along with its modifications; udāhṛtam—is described.
verses.translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate bodily organism (Sanghata), mental consciousness, and fortitude—this, in brief, constitutes the Field along with its modifications.
verses.meaning: Remarkably, Sri Krishna includes psychological states—desire (Iccha), aversion (Dvesha), pleasure (Sukha), sorrow (Duhkha), bodily cohesion (Sanghata), cognitive awareness (Chetana), and fortitude (Dhriti)—as parts of the Field! The mind and emotions are subtle matter, objects of consciousness, not consciousness itself. The true Self (Kshetrajna) is the changeless witness of all mental emotions and bodily states.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् |
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् |
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam |
ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: amānitvam—humility/absence of pride; adambhitvam—unpretentiousness/freedom from hypocrisy; ahiṃsā—non-violence/harmlessness; kṣāntiḥ—forgiveness/patience; ārjavam—uprightness/straightforwardness; ācārya-upāsanam—service to the spiritual master; śaucam—purity of body and mind; sthairyam—steadfastness; ātma-vinigrahaḥ—self-control.
verses.translation: Humility, freedom from hypocrisy, non-violence, patience, straightforwardness, service to the spiritual preceptor, internal and external purity, steadfastness, and self-control;
verses.meaning: In Verses 8 through 12, Sri Krishna defines 'Jnana' (Knowledge) not as academic information, but as the twenty moral and spiritual virtues that cleanse the mind and allow the light of the Self to shine. Here the Lord lists Amanitvam (humility), Adambhitvam (simplicity), Ahimsa (universal non-harming), Kshanti (patience), Arjavam (integrity), Acharyopasanam (reverence for the Guru), Shaucam (cleanliness), Sthairyam (unshakable purpose), and Atma-vinigraha (restraint of the lower self).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च |
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च |
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम् || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca |
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: indriya-artheṣu—in the objects of the senses; vairāgyam—dispassion/renunciation; anahaṅkāraḥ—absence of egoism/pride; eva ca—and also; janma—birth; mṛtyu—death; jarā—old age; vyādhi—disease; duḥkha—misery; doṣa—defects/faults; anudarśanam—repeated perception/reflection.
verses.translation: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses, absence of egoism, and constant perception of the inherent suffering and defects in birth, death, old age, and disease;
verses.meaning: Real spiritual awakening requires seeing worldly existence with clarity. By meditating upon the four fundamental realities of mortal embodiment—Janma (birth), Mrityu (death), Jara (old age), and Vyadhi (disease)—one cultivates profound dispassion (Vairagya) and dissolves the illusion of permanent material happiness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु |
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
असक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु |
नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
asaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu |
nityaṃ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: asaktiḥ—non-attachment; anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ—absence of clinging identification; putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu—with children, spouse, home, and possessions; nityam—always; ca—and; sama-cittatvam—equanimity of mind; iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapattiṣu—in the occurrence of desirable and undesirable events.
verses.translation: Non-attachment, freedom from excessive clinging to children, spouse, home, and possessions, and constant equanimity of mind in the occurrence of both desirable and undesirable events;
verses.meaning: Anabhishvanga denotes freedom from obsessive codependency and possessiveness. One loves and serves family responsibly as a duty to God, but does not lose one's spiritual equilibrium, maintaining serene equanimity whether circumstances turn out favorable or unfavorable.

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी |
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी |
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī |
viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: mayi—unto Me; ca—and; ananya-yogena—by undivided yoga/focus; bhaktiḥ—devotion; avyabhicāriṇī—unswerving/unalloyed; vivikta-deśa-sevitvam—preference for secluded and holy places; aratiḥ—distaste/lack of desire; jana-saṃsadi—for the society of worldly crowds.
verses.translation: Unswerving, unalloyed devotion unto Me through exclusive yoga, a fondness for quiet and contemplative places, and a natural distaste for worldly gatherings;
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reveals that pure devotion (Avyabhicarini Bhakti) is the crowning jewel of true wisdom. Jnana without devotion becomes dry intellectualism, while devotion grounded in discriminative wisdom leads to the highest realization. Seeking holy solitude (Vivikta-desha) nourishes quiet introspection and deep meditation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् |
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम् |
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोऽन्यथा || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam |
etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadato'nyathā || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam—constancy in spiritual knowledge of the Self; tattva-jñāna-artha-darśanam—perception of the ultimate goal of philosophical wisdom (liberation/God); etat—all this; jñānam—knowledge; iti—thus; proktam—is declared; ajñānam—ignorance; yat—whatever; ataḥ anyathā—is contrary to this.
verses.translation: Constancy in self-knowledge, and realization of the ultimate goal of metaphysical truth—all this is declared to be true Knowledge (Jnana); whatever is contrary to this is Ignorance (Ajnana).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna concludes His 20-virtue definition of Knowledge. Any learning, science, or technology that does not lead to self-mastery, inner peace, and divine realization is categorized as 'Ajnana' (ignorance) because it binds the soul more tightly to the wheel of samsara.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते |
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते |
अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvāmṛtamaśnute |
anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: jñeyam—the object to be known; yat—which; tat—that; pravakṣyāmi—I shall fully declare; yat—which; jñātvā—knowing; amṛtam—immortality; aśnute—one attains/experiences; anādi-mat—the beginningless; param brahma—the Supreme Brahman; na—neither; sat—being/existent; tat—that; na—nor; asat—non-being; ucyate—is said to be.
verses.translation: I shall now describe that which is to be known (Jneya), by realizing which one attains immortality. It is the Supreme Brahman, beginningless and without origin, which is said to be neither Sat (existence) nor Asat (non-existence).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna turns to 'Jneya'—the ultimate Object of Knowledge, Parabrahman. Realizing this Truth bestows immortality (Amritam). Brahman is described as neither 'Sat' (matter with manifest form and name) nor 'Asat' (unmanifest potential), because It is the transcendental Conscious Ground upon which both sat and asat appear.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् |
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् |
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham |
sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarvataḥ—everywhere; pāṇi-pādam—with hands and feet; tat—That (Brahman); sarvataḥ—everywhere; akṣi-śiraḥ-mukham—with eyes, heads, and faces; sarvataḥ—everywhere; śrutimat—with ears; loke—in the universe; sarvam—everything; āvṛtya—enveloping/pervading; tiṣṭhati—exists.
verses.translation: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, with ears on all sides in the universe—That (Supreme Being) exists, all-pervading and enveloping everything.
verses.meaning: This iconic Upanishadic verse (echoing the Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.16) depicts the cosmic omnipresence of Brahman. Every hand that works, every foot that walks, every eye that sees, and every ear that hears in any living creature operates by the borrowed light and power of the one indwelling Supreme Consciousness.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् |
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् |
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam |
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsam—illuminating the functions of all the senses; sarva-indriya-vivarjitam—yet completely devoid of physical senses; asaktam—unattached; sarva-bhṛt—the sustainer of all; ca eva—and also; nirguṇam—transcending the three gunas (modes); guṇa-bhoktṛ—the experiencer of the gunas; ca—and.
verses.translation: Illuminating the functions of all sensory organs, yet devoid of all physical senses; unattached, yet the sustainer of all creation; free from the material modes (Nirguna), yet the master experiencer of the modes;
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna presents the divine paradox of Brahman. The Divine perceives everything without physical sensory organs (just as pure awareness illuminates sight, hearing, and thought), sustains all cosmic forms without becoming entangled or limited by them, and transcends all material qualities while presiding as their supreme lord.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च |
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च |
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca |
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: bahiḥ—outside; antaḥ—inside; ca—and; bhūtānām—of all living beings; acaram—unmoving; caram—moving; eva ca—and also; sūkṣmatvāt—due to subtlety; tat—That; avijñeyam—incomprehensible/unknowable to senses; dūrastham—far away; ca—and; antike—near; ca—and; tat—That.
verses.translation: Existing both outside and inside all beings, unmoving yet moving; due to Its subtlety, It is incomprehensible to the senses; It is far away, yet exceedingly near.
verses.meaning: Brahman is all-pervading: It is inside as the indwelling Self (Antaryamin) and outside as the fabric of the universe. To the ignorant who look only outward, God seems infinitely distant (Durastham); but to the awakened devotee who looks within, God is nearer than breath itself (Antike).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् |
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् |
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam |
bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: avibhaktam—undivided; ca—and; bhūteṣu—among all living beings; vibhaktam iva—as if divided; ca—and; sthitam—situated; bhūta-bhartṛ—the sustainer of all beings; ca—and; tat—That; jñeyam—to be known; grasiṣṇu—the devourer (at dissolution); prabhaviṣṇu—the generator/creator; ca—and.
verses.translation: Undivided, yet appearing situated as if divided among all beings; That Supreme Reality is to be known as the sustainer of beings (Sthiti), the devourer (Laya), and the creator (Srishti).
verses.meaning: Just as space appears partitioned by walls into rooms but remains indivisible one space, or the single sun reflects in millions of water vessels, so the One Supreme Consciousness appears divided in countless bodies. It is the sole origin, preserver, and ultimate resting place of the universe.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते |
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते |
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: jyotiṣām api—even of all lights; tat—That; jyotiḥ—the supreme Light; tamasaḥ—darkness of ignorance; param—beyond; ucyate—is said to be; jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; jñāna-gamyam—the goal to be attained by knowledge; hṛdi—in the heart; sarvasya—of all beings; viṣṭhitam—seated/abiding.
verses.translation: That is the Light of all lights, declared to be beyond the darkness of ignorance. It is Knowledge, the Object of Knowledge, and the Goal attained by Knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.
verses.meaning: Brahman is Jyotisham Jyotih—the self-luminous Source from which the sun, moon, stars, and fire derive their brilliance (Katha Upanishad 2.2.15). Crucially, this infinite transcendent Light does not dwell in some distant cosmic heaven, but is seated directly within the spiritual heart (Hridi Sarvasya Vishthitam) of every living entity.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः |
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः |
मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: iti—thus; kṣetram—the field; tathā—as well as; jñānam—knowledge; jñeyam—the object of knowledge; ca—and; uktam—have been spoken; samāsataḥ—in brief; mat-bhaktaḥ—My devotee; etat—this; vijñāya—understanding deeply; mat-bhāvāya—for My divine nature / state of being; upapadyate—becomes qualified/attains.
verses.translation: Thus the Field (Kshetra), Knowledge (Jnana), and the Object of Knowledge (Jneya) have been briefly described. My devotee, understanding this deeply, attains to My Divine Nature (Mad-bhava).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna summarizes the first half of Chapter 13. He emphasizes that the fruit of this philosophical wisdom is attained by the devotee (Madbhakta). When devotion and non-dual wisdom unite, the soul transcends mortal limitations and participates in God's divine eternal nature.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि |
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान् || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि |
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान् || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi |
vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisambhavān || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: prakṛtim—material nature; puruṣam—the conscious spirit; ca eva—and also; viddhi—know; anādī—beginningless; ubhau api—both of them; vikārān—modifications/transformations; ca—and; guṇān—the three modes (gunas); ca eva—and also; viddhi—know; prakṛti-sambhavān—born of material nature.
verses.translation: Know that both Prakriti (material nature) and Purusha (the conscious spirit) are beginningless. Know also that all bodily modifications and the three modes of nature (gunas) are born of Prakriti.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna now elucidates Prakriti and Purusha. Both are eternal potencies of the Supreme Lord without a chronological beginning. All physical transformations (body, organs, mind) and the psychological play of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas arise strictly within the domain of Prakriti.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कार्यकरणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते |
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते || २१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कार्यकरणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते |
पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kāryakaraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate |
puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate || 21 ||
verses.word_meanings: kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve—in the creation of effect (the body) and cause/instruments (the senses); hetuḥ—the cause/agent; prakṛtiḥ—material nature; ucyate—is said to be; puruṣaḥ—the conscious soul; sukha-duḥkhānām—of pleasures and pains; bhoktṛtve—in the experience/enjoyment; hetuḥ—the cause; ucyate—is said to be.
verses.translation: Prakriti is said to be the cause of the physical body and sensory instruments of action; the Purusha (conscious spirit) is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain.
verses.meaning: Prakriti produces the physical organism and sensory apparatus that perform all physical deeds. The Purusha, by virtue of consciousness, experiences the resultant joys and sorrows when it mistakenly identifies with the body.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् |
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु || २२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् |
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān |
kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu || 22 ||
verses.word_meanings: puruṣaḥ—the conscious spirit/soul; prakṛti-sthaḥ—situated in material nature; hi—indeed; bhuṅkte—experiences/enjoys; prakṛti-jān—born of material nature; guṇān—the modes (gunas); kāraṇam—the cause; guṇa-saṅgaḥ—attachment to the modes; asya—of this soul; sat-asat-yoni-janmasu—in good and evil wombs/births.
verses.translation: For the Purusha, dwelling in material nature, experiences the modes (gunas) born of Prakriti. Attachment to these modes is the cause of its rebirth in higher and lower wombs.
verses.meaning: The soul itself is pure, divine, and free. However, when it associates with Prakriti and becomes attached (Guna-sanga) to worldly desires, it generates karmic momentum that compels it to take birth repeatedly in various species and circumstances according to its dominant gunas.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः |
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः || २३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः |
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |
paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ || 23 ||
verses.word_meanings: upadraṣṭā—the spectator/witness; anumantā—the permitter; ca—and; bhartā—the sustainer; bhoktā—the experiencer; mahā-īśvaraḥ—the Great Lord; parama-ātmā—the Supreme Self; iti—thus; ca api—and also; uktaḥ—is designated; dehe asmin—in this body; puruṣaḥ paraḥ—the Transcendental Spirit.
verses.translation: The impartial Witness (Upadrashta), the Permitter (Anumanta), the Sustainer (Bharta), the Experiencer (Bhokta), the Great Lord (Maheshvara), and the Supreme Self (Paramatman)—thus is the Supreme Spirit within this body declared.
verses.meaning: This master verse outlines the sixfold relationship of the Supreme Lord (Paramatman) within the human body: Upadrashta (the silent, all-seeing witness), Anumanta (the permitter who allows free will to operate), Bharta (the life-sustaining power), Bhokta (the ultimate consumer of devotional offerings), Maheshvara (the sovereign cosmic ruler), and Paramatman (the transcendent non-dual Self).
verses.purport: This master verse outlines the sixfold relationship of the Supreme Lord (Paramatman) within the human body: Upadrashta (the silent, all-seeing witness), Anumanta (the permitter who allows free will to operate), Bharta (the life-sustaining power), Bhokta (the ultimate consumer of devotional offerings), Maheshvara (the sovereign cosmic ruler), and Paramatman (the transcendent non-dual Self).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह |
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते || २४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह |
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha |
sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate || 24 ||
verses.word_meanings: yaḥ—whoever; evam—thus; vetti—knows/realizes; puruṣam—the conscious Spirit; prakṛtim—material nature; ca—and; guṇaiḥ saha—along with the modes (gunas); sarvathā—in all ways/circumstances; vartamānaḥ api—though living and acting; na—not; saḥ—he; bhūyaḥ—again; abhijāyate—is reborn.
verses.translation: He who thus understands the Purusha (Spirit) and Prakriti (Nature) along with the gunas, in whatever condition he may live, is never born again into mortal bondage.
verses.meaning: Direct intuitive realization of the distinction between matter (Prakriti) and the immortal Spirit (Purusha) dissolves the root ignorance (Avidya) that causes reincarnation. Such a liberated sage (Jivanmukta) acts in the world free from karmic attachment and attains Moksha upon leaving the body.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना |
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे || २५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना |
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā |
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare || 25 ||
verses.word_meanings: dhyānena—by deep meditation; ātmani—within the heart/self; paśyanti—behold/perceive; kecit—some; ātmānam—the Supreme Self; ātmanā—by the purified mind/intellect; anye—others; sāṅkhyena yogena—by the yoga of philosophical discrimination (Jnana); karma-yogena—by the yoga of selfless action; ca apare—and still others.
verses.translation: Some perceive the indwelling Self in the heart through meditation by the purified mind; others through the philosophical discrimination of Sankhya Yoga; and others through the practice of Karma Yoga.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna honors the diverse temperaments of spiritual seekers: The contemplative mystic attains God through Raja Yoga / Dhyana (meditation); the intellectual seeker through Sankhya / Jnana Yoga (philosophical inquiry); and the active personality through Karma Yoga (selfless dedicated service).
verses.purport: Sri Krishna honors the diverse temperaments of spiritual seekers: The contemplative mystic attains God through Raja Yoga / Dhyana (meditation); the intellectual seeker through Sankhya / Jnana Yoga (philosophical inquiry); and the active personality through Karma Yoga (selfless dedicated service).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते |
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः || २६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते |
तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate |
te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ || 26 ||
verses.word_meanings: anye—others; tu—yet; evam—thus; ajānantaḥ—not knowing these yogic paths; śrutvā—having heard; anyebhyaḥ—from realized teachers/sages; upāsate—worship/practice; te api—they also; ca—and; atitaranti—transcend/cross over; eva—certainly; mṛtyum—death/mortality; śruti-parāyaṇāḥ—devoted to what they have heard.
verses.translation: Yet others, unacquainted with these yogic paths, worship having heard from enlightened masters. They too certainly cross beyond death, steadfastly devoted to the sacred truths they have heard.
verses.meaning: In His boundless compassion, Sri Krishna assures that even seekers without deep philosophical erudition or yogic expertise can attain liberation simply through sincere faith in the words of enlightened saints (Shruti-parayanah) and authentic devotion.
verses.purport: In His boundless compassion, Sri Krishna assures that even seekers without deep philosophical erudition or yogic expertise can attain liberation simply through sincere faith in the words of enlightened saints (Shruti-parayanah) and authentic devotion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ || २७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yāvatsañjāyate kiñcitsattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam |
kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha || 27 ||
verses.word_meanings: yāvat—whatever; sañjāyate—is born/produced; kiñcit—anything; sattvam—living entity/existence; sthāvara-jaṅgamam—unmoving (plant/mineral) or moving (animal/human); kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogāt—from the union of the field and the knower of the field; tat—that; viddhi—know; bharata-ṛṣabha—O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Whatever entity comes into existence, whether moving or unmoving, know that, O bull of the Bharatas, to be produced entirely from the union of the Field (Kshetra) and the Knower of the Field (Kshetrajna).
verses.meaning: Every manifestation in creation—from a blade of grass to a galaxy, from an insect to an archangel—is an interplay of inert matter (Kshetra) animated by the conscious spirit (Kshetrajna).
verses.purport: Every manifestation in creation—from a blade of grass to a galaxy, from an insect to an archangel—is an interplay of inert matter (Kshetra) animated by the conscious spirit (Kshetrajna).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् |
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति || २८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् |
विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram |
vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati || 28 ||
verses.word_meanings: samam—equally; sarveṣu—in all; bhūteṣu—living beings; tiṣṭhantam—dwelling; parama-īśvaram—the Supreme Lord; vinaśyatsu—among the perishable bodies; avinaśyantam—the Imperishable Spirit; yaḥ—whoever; paśyati—sees; saḥ—he; paśyati—truly sees.
verses.translation: He who sees the Supreme Lord dwelling equally in all living beings—the Imperishable amidst the perishable—he alone truly sees.
verses.meaning: True vision (Samyak Darshana) consists not in observing external physical diversity, but in beholding the one immortal Divine Presence (Parameshvara) shining identically within every creature amid the birth, change, and decay of bodily forms.
verses.purport: True vision (Samyak Darshana) consists not in observing external physical diversity, but in beholding the one immortal Divine Presence (Parameshvara) shining identically within every creature amid the birth, change, and decay of bodily forms.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् |
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् || २९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् |
न हिनस्त्यात्मनात्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
samaṃ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram |
na hinastyātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim || 29 ||
verses.word_meanings: samam—equally; paśyan—seeing; hi—indeed; sarvatra—everywhere; samavasthitam—equally situated; īśvaram—the Lord; na—not; hinasti—injures/degrades; ātmanā—by the mind; ātmānam—the Self; tataḥ—thereby; yāti—attains; parām—the supreme; gatim—goal/destination.
verses.translation: Seeing the same Lord equally present everywhere, he does not degrade the higher Self through the lower egoic mind; and thereby he attains the Supreme Destination.
verses.meaning: When one recognizes God in all beings, one cannot harm another without harming oneself. The destructive ego is neutralized by universal vision, leading the practitioner directly to supreme liberation (Param Gatim).
verses.purport: When one recognizes God in all beings, one cannot harm another without harming oneself. The destructive ego is neutralized by universal vision, leading the practitioner directly to supreme liberation (Param Gatim).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः |
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति || ३० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः |
यः पश्यति तथात्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
yaḥ paśyati tathātmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati || 30 ||
verses.word_meanings: prakṛtyā eva—by material nature alone; ca—and; karmāṇi—all actions; kriyamāṇāni—being performed; sarvaśaḥ—in every way; yaḥ—whoever; paśyati—sees; tathā—also; ātmānam—the Self; akartāram—as the non-doer; saḥ—he; paśyati—truly sees.
verses.translation: He who perceives that all actions in every respect are being performed by Prakriti (material nature) alone, and that the Self is the non-doer (Akartar)—he truly sees.
verses.meaning: The pure Atman is actionless, changeless awareness. It is the gunas and energy of Prakriti that interact, move, speak, and work. The sage who witnesses nature operating without falsely assuming 'I am the doer' is liberated from karmic bondage.
verses.purport: The pure Atman is actionless, changeless awareness. It is the gunas and energy of Prakriti that interact, move, speak, and work. The sage who witnesses nature operating without falsely assuming 'I am the doer' is liberated from karmic bondage.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति |
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा || ३१ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति |
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा || ३१ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati |
tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma sampadyate tadā || 31 ||
verses.word_meanings: yadā—when; bhūta-pṛthak-bhāvam—the diversified existence of all living beings; eka-stham—rooted in the One; anupaśyati—perceives/realizes; tataḥ eva—from That alone; ca—and; vistāram—the expansion/manifold manifestation; brahma—Brahman; sampadyate—attains; tadā—then.
verses.translation: When one perceives the diversified existence of all living beings rooted in the One, and their cosmic expansion from That alone, one then attains unity with Brahman.
verses.meaning: Just as waves of countless shapes and sizes are nothing but water, and gold ornaments are nothing but gold, all diverse living entities are rooted in the one unbroken ocean of Brahman. Realizing this essential oneness is the attainment of Brahman (Brahma-sampatti).
verses.purport: Just as waves of countless shapes and sizes are nothing but water, and gold ornaments are nothing but gold, all diverse living entities are rooted in the one unbroken ocean of Brahman. Realizing this essential oneness is the attainment of Brahman (Brahma-sampatti).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः |
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते || ३२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः |
शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते || ३२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmāyamavyayaḥ |
śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate || 32 ||
verses.word_meanings: anāditvāt—due to being beginningless; nirguṇatvāt—due to being free from material qualities/gunas; parama-ātmā—the Supreme Self; ayam—this; avyayaḥ—imperishable; śarīra-sthaḥ api—even though dwelling in the body; kaunteya—O son of Kunti (Arjuna); na—neither; karoti—acts; na—nor; lipyate—is tainted/affected.
verses.translation: Being beginningless and free from the material modes (Nirguna), this imperishable Supreme Self, though dwelling within the physical body, O Kaunteya, neither acts nor is tainted.
verses.meaning: Because the Atman has no origin and is unconditioned by the three gunas, it is intrinsically untainted by the sickness, aging, sins, or virtues of the physical body in which it resides, just as sunlight illuminating a mirror is never affected by dirt on the glass.
verses.purport: Because the Atman has no origin and is unconditioned by the three gunas, it is intrinsically untainted by the sickness, aging, sins, or virtues of the physical body in which it resides, just as sunlight illuminating a mirror is never affected by dirt on the glass.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते |
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते || ३३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते |
सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथात्मा नोपलिप्यते || ३३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate |
sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate || 33 ||
verses.word_meanings: yathā—as; sarva-gatam—all-pervading; saukṣmyāt—due to subtlety; ākāśam—space/ether; na—not; upalipyate—is tainted/stained; sarvatra—everywhere; avasthitaḥ—situated; dehe—in the body; tathā—so; ātmā—the Self; na—not; upalipyate—is tainted.
verses.translation: Just as the all-pervading space (Akasha), owing to its subtlety, is not tainted by anything it contains, so the Self, stationed everywhere in the body, is never tainted.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna provides a sublime metaphor: Space is present inside pure flowers as well as mud, yet space is neither fragranced by the flower nor dirtied by the mud. Similarly, the pure Atman permeates every cell of the physical body without absorbing its material taints.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna provides a sublime metaphor: Space is present inside pure flowers as well as mud, yet space is neither fragranced by the flower nor dirtied by the mud. Similarly, the pure Atman permeates every cell of the physical body without absorbing its material taints.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः |
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत || ३४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः |
क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत || ३४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ |
kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata || 34 ||
verses.word_meanings: yathā—as; prakāśayati—illuminates; ekaḥ—the one; kṛtsnam—the entire; lokam—world/solar system; imam—this; raviḥ—sun; kṣetram—the field (body/mind); kṣetrī—the Knower of the Field; tathā—so; kṛtsnam—the entire; prakāśayati—illuminates; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.translation: Just as the single sun illuminates this entire cosmic world, so does the Knower of the Field (Kshetrin) illuminate the whole Field with conscious awareness, O Bharata.
verses.meaning: A second luminous metaphor: One sun illumines all continents, oceans, and living beings without becoming tainted by what it shines upon. In the same way, the one Conscious Knower (Kshetrin/Atman) illumines all perceptions, thoughts, emotions, and sensations across the entire Field of human experience.
verses.purport: A second luminous metaphor: One sun illumines all continents, oceans, and living beings without becoming tainted by what it shines upon. verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा |
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् || ३५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा |
भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् || ३५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā |
bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param || 35 ||
verses.word_meanings: kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ—between the field and the knower of the field; evam—thus; antaram—the distinction/difference; jñāna-cakṣuṣā—by the eye of spiritual wisdom; bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣam—the liberation of living beings from material nature (Prakriti); ca—and; ye—those who; viduḥ—know/realize; yānti—attain; te—they; param—the Supreme Goal.
verses.translation: Those who perceive with the eye of wisdom (Jnana Chakshu) this distinction between the Field (Kshetra) and the Knower of the Field (Kshetrajna), and comprehend the liberation of living beings from material nature—they attain the Supreme.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna crowns the thirteenth chapter with this liberating promise. By cultivating the 'Eye of Wisdom' (Jnana Chakshu), one directly discriminates between the perishable body-mind complex and the eternal conscious Soul, ending all identification with material nature and attaining supreme transcendental liberation (Param).
